note: Curated catalog of open source (open-weight) video generation models, verified via web search Aug 2026. Model ids are Hugging Face repo ids intended for DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained. VRAM figures are sourced from model cards/community benchmarks and vary with resolution/frame count/offloading; treat as approximate. Excluded: ByteDance Waver 1.0 — ranks top-3 on public leaderboards but is confirmed NOT open-weight (code/paper public, trained weights proprietary), so it doesn't belong in this catalog.

minimal.description: Entry-level/laptop GPU. Native video DiT models are not viable here; only SD-based motion-module approaches (AnimateDiff) work.

low.description: Single consumer GPU, e.g. RTX 3060/4060/4070 class.

mid.description: High-end consumer/prosumer GPU, e.g. RTX 4090/5090, L4/L40S class.

high.description: Datacenter GPU or multi-GPU, e.g. A100/H100 80GB class.

animatediff.license: Apache-2.0 (repo tag); project README states "released for academic use" — verify before commercial use
animatediff.notes: Not a native video model — a motion module applied on top of SD1.5. 16 frames, 512x512 native. The only viable option below 8GB VRAM; noticeably behind DiT-based models on coherence and resolution.

magi_1_distilled.notes: Autoregressive chunk-based generation (predicts fixed-length video chunks sequentially, next chunk starts before current fully denoises) rather than single-shot diffusion — designed to hold up better over longer/more dynamic motion than same-tier single-shot models. 12GB figure requires window_size=1 in the distill+quant config.

wan2.1_1.3b.notes: Smallest member of the Wan family, explicitly built for consumer GPUs.

cogvideox_2b.notes: Smaller sibling of CogVideoX-5B. Trained in FP16; quantizable further with PytorchAO/Optimum-quanto down to free-tier-Colab-class GPUs.

ltx_video.notes: Optimized for speed; near-real-time generation. Community reports usable down to 6GB with quantization/offloading and reduced resolution, but 12GB is the realistic floor for normal use.

wan2.2_ti2v_5b.notes: Unified T2V+I2V in one checkpoint. ~27.4GB at FP16 for 25 frames @ 768x512; FP8 cuts ~40%. Very fast — a 5s 720p clip in under 9 minutes on a single consumer GPU.

cogvideox_5b.notes: Well documented, mature diffusers support, good quality/resource balance. Trained in BF16.

hunyuanvideo_1_5.notes: Top-tier quality at a deliberately lowered parameter count; tuned to run on consumer-grade GPUs. Up to 15s clips at 24fps, 720p.

wan2.2_a14b.params: 27B total / 14B active per step (MoE: high-noise + low-noise experts)
wan2.2_a14b.notes: First open source MoE video model. Default requires an 80GB-class GPU (A100/H100); --offload_model/--t5_cpu flags trade speed for lower VRAM but 80GB is the no-compromise figure.

mochi_1.notes: Very strong motion quality/coherence. ~60-70GB single-GPU at full precision for the full 163-frame length; the bf16 variant with ComfyUI-level optimization can run under 22GB, at reduced frame count/speed.

skyreels_v1.notes: Fine-tuned from HunyuanVideo on ~10M film/TV clips; best open option for human-centric cinematic quality (faces, expression, camera work).

magi_1_full.notes: Full, non-distilled version. Exact VRAM floor not confirmed via search; scaling from the 4.5B variant's ~24GB at standard precision implies an 80GB+ class requirement. Same autoregressive chunk-based architecture as magi_1_distilled, at full quality.

ltx_2_5.notes: Only open model with native audio+video generation in a single pass (dual-stream DiT with cross-modal attention). ~66GB at full precision; FP8 quantization brings it to ~30-35GB (48GB cards viable); community FP8+CPU-offload builds report running on 16-24GB cards at a further speed cost.

action.note: minimal tier is not viable — action's fast/complex motion is exactly what AnimateDiff's SD1.5 motion module handles worst.

ugc_product_review.note: Use each model's image-to-video variant, conditioned on reference_image, when product fidelity matters.

commercial_product_ad.note: Use each model's image-to-video variant, conditioned on reference_image, when product fidelity matters.

presenter_avatar.note: Only ltx_2_5 generates dialogue as native synced audio (mid tier uses its ~30GB FP8-quantized path). At the low tier, dialogue/voice_tone must be produced by a separate TTS + lip-sync step layered on top of ltx_video's silent output.

social_short_form_ad.note: Same native-audio caveat as presenter_avatar for the low tier.

music_video.note: ltx_2_5 (FP8-quantized at mid, ~30GB) is the only model in this catalog with native audio sync. No model here fits below ~30GB, so there is no low/minimal option for this type at all.

motion_graphics.note: No model in this catalog targets abstract/graphic motion-design output; entries here are the fastest-iteration fallback, not a genuine fit.
